title: Tengu Hog Tie
description: In this class, Gestalta teaches a floor-based predicament with their model Olivia.
about:
In this class, Gestalta teaches a floor-based predicament with their model Olivia.

This hogtie with a twist starts off with a crotch rope incorporated directly into a tight Tengu chest tie. The ankles and hair are then tied into the back to create a severe hog tie position. Expect some panting, struggling and moaning!

Please note that this class is not suited for beginners, even if it is floor-based. The Tengu shown in this class is quite minimalistic and threatening to the nerves and strict hog tie positions can be a real challenge for bottoms due to the breathing restrictions and intense back bending. There is another class available on the site for a less severe version of the hog tie, which is suitable for beginners.

Feel free to use a different chest harness and adjust any part of the tie to fit your own preferences and skills. You can replace the hair rope with a rope gag if needed.

title: Uplines & Lock-Offs 101 (Free)
description: Gorgone teaches the most common methods for attaching a suspension line onto a limb or a harness and how to lock and unlock it safely.
about:
In this free shibari course, Gorgone teaches the most common methods for attaching a suspension upline onto a limb or a harness as well as how to lock it off safely.

This 10-video course covers basic anchoring techniques, upper and lower locks on rings and bamboos, various locks and finishing options, general safety advice and weight handling.

Please note the importance of practicing these techniques with heavy props or on yourself before suspending a partner. Start with partial suspensions and make sure to build automatism, flow and speed with your lines before doing full suspensions.

We recommend watching and practicing the videos in the right order. Suspensions should be monitored by a skilled spotter and never attempted or performed alone until your skills and experience are truly reliable.

*Captions available for this series: English
safety: This course is designed to introduce or refresh knowledge of suspension points safety, and upline techniques. It is best practice to be confident in your harness building and floor play before diving into suspension.

title: Gorgone's Hip Harness
description: Designed from a model's perspective, this Hip-Harness is very well suited for self-suspensions and dynamic suspensions and transitions.
about:
GO TO GORGONE’S HIP HARNESS GUIDE

In this class, Gorgone teaches her original Hip Harness with her model Becky. Designed from a model's perspective, this Hip-Harness is very well suited for dynamic self-suspensions and partnered suspensions and transitions.

The original tie is particularly well suited for bottoms with more flexibility in the lower back and those who enjoy waist-loaded harnesses. The "wide front" variation demoed on her model Aja is designed to remove all pressure from the waist and lower back for bottoms who prefer hip-loaded harnesses.

The very compact frontal stem gives this harness a very balanced distribution of the load between the three supportive layers and makes it very resistant to dynamic movements in suspension. The placements and tensions are designed to make it as comfortable as possible for inversions and bridge poses.

In the suspension line video, Gorgone shows how to create a stable anchor point. In the Self Suspension class, she demonstrates exercises to help gain confidence and autonomy in a Hip-Harnesses.

The demo video is a straightforward version of the same tie without talking. It is useful to overview the harness before studying the tutorial or to refresh your memory after you have watched the tutorial with full explanations.

title: Kinoko’s Maete Harness
description: In this shibari course, Kinoko teaches the suspendable Maete harness with his model hua hua, offering a hands-front alternative to TKs.
about:
In this shibari course, Kinoko teaches the suspendable Maete harness with his model hua hua.

While behind-the-back box-ties and variations on the TK may be the more traditional options for a suspendable harness, placing the hands in front of the body can make for greater comfort and sustainability. Kinoko’s Maete tie offers a hands-front harness built for face-up suspensions with plenty of supportive wraps in the back and a stable and sturdy structure in the point for attaching your suspension line.

In the first class, Kinoko offers a step-by-step demonstration for how to tie the Maete harness.

In the second class, you’ll learn how to add a hip harness that will offer even more stability in the suspension to follow.

In the final class, Kinoko demonstrates how to suspend the tie, explaining how certain lines can be raised or lowered based on your model’s needs to increase sustainability.

This course is great for expanding your harness repertoire and for learners looking for alternative to TKs. However, please keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from these classes and only use this harness in suspension if that is already a part of your rope practice.

*Captions available for this class: English
safety: This course utilizes suspension lines to create the final form. Before attempting, you’ll need to first familiarize yourself with safe suspension line technique and with the harnesses being used. As rope crosses the arms in this course, we suggest the person being tied be familiar with how to check their hands for signs of nerve compression. If you are newer to suspension, please only suspend with a spotter nearby or with the supervision of a qualified instructor.
equipment: At least six hanks of rope

title: Kneeling Predicament
description: In-depth tutorial for Gestalta's kneeling predicament including a hair tie.
about:
In this class, Gestalta teaches a simple floor-based predicament with their model Olivia.

A strategically placed hair tie is used to force the model to shift their weight onto their tied-up toes for maximum effect. You can feel free to replace the hair-tie with a rope gag for this predicament.

If you are looking for a fun and challenging tie without using too much rope or technique and no suspension point, this class is for you!

This predicament is suitable for beginners as well as more experienced practitioners.

title: Gorgone's TK
description: In this class Gorgone teaches her original TK designed for more comfortable face-down suspensions and torsions.
about:
In this class Gorgone teaches the basic and third-rope pattern of her original TK on her models Joann and Aja.

The stemless back structure make this TK particularly suited for models who prefer a high placement for the lower wraps. Its compact and solid stem allows for the creation of a circular anchor point in the back for more comfortable face-downs and torsions and makes it very resistant to stress in dynamic transitions.

In the suspension lines video Gorgone explains how to create anchor points in the back, side and front of the harness.

The demo video is a straightforward version of the same tie without talking. It is useful to understand the harness before studying the tutorial or to refresh your memory after you have watched the tutorial with full explanations.
safety: This is a harness course that requires the understanding of simple frictions and forms. It’s best practice to incorporate harnesses into your play only after you can tie them by memory. As rope crosses the arms in this course, we suggest the person being tied be familiar with how to check their hands for signs of nerve compression.
equipment: At least two hanks of rope

title: Kata Ashi Sequence
description: Gestalta's 'Kata-Ashi' transition sequence masterclass.
about:
In this course Gestalta teaches one of their self-developed show routines with their model Evitrii.

This challenging transition sequence starts with a dynamic transition from a face-down to a Kata-Ashi position (one leg up vertical suspension) and evolves into a total of seven positions.

The 'Fast Futo' and 'Half-Basket Tie' used by Gestalta in this sequence are taught in separate videos and should be practiced and mastered before studying the full transition class.

The sequence and harnesses can be modified to suit your partner's needs and preferences or according to your own style and creativity. We recommend watching the full sequence class thoroughly before practicing yourself.

The last demo video showcases the same sequence without talking. It is useful for inspiration or to see Gestalta tie with flow and to remember the order of all positions and transitions after you have studied the class with full explanations.

We always suggest learning new sequences with the support of a spotter or with the supervision of a qualified instructor. As rope crosses the arms in this course, we suggest the person being tied be familiar with how to check their hands for signs of nerve compression.

title: Half-Mermaid
description: In this shibari class, Lief and Icky teach their version of the Half-Mermaid harness, as well as demonstrating how to suspend it.
about:
In this shibari class, Lief and Icky teach their version of the Half-Mermaid harness, as well as demonstrating how to suspend it.

Binding the legs together from the waist to just above the knees, the Half-Mermaid harness is a great alternative to a booty basket or hip harness: suspendable, supportive and ultra-snug. Lief and Icky’s take on the tie builds in additional lower back support as well as extra cinches to prevent the rope from traveling into the nervy knee pit area. As Lief explains, no band is purely decorative – every rope is placed intentionally and to offer support.

In the first part of the class, they teach the step-by-step Half-Mermaid pattern, detailing important safety tips, including how best to keep the bottom stable as you tie and how to avoid impinging on the nerves and tendons in the back of the knees. They also offer guidelines for how to ensure the correct tension before attempting to suspend the tie.

In the second part of the class, you’ll learn where and how to load the Half-Mermaid tie, and from there, how to suspend it.

This course is great if you’re looking to level up your lower body harnesses and learn some new leg tie variants. However, please keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from these classes and only use this harness in suspension if that is already a part of your rope practice.

title: Breaking Patterns Game
description: In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches the Breaking Patterns Game with her model Cutebutdeadly.
about:
In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches the Breaking Patterns Game with her model Cutebutdeadly – an improvisational tying-with-a-twist exercise to play your way out of ropey ruts.

If you frequently find yourself repeating the same sequences in rope or struggling to discover new shapes in partial suspensions, Kissmedeadlydoll has got a game for you. Created for rope students already comfortable with suspensions and body manipulation, the Breaking Patterns Game adopts a “fuck-around-and-find-out” attitude to encourage you to explore new and different options as you tie. Play this game frequently and remember to “deny yourself access to the first choice you would make”.

In the first part of this course, Kissmedeadlydoll highlights some important rules and considerations for the game. This includes how to start and how to progress, disregarding your Choice A and maybe even Choice B to introduce more experimentation to your rope.

In the next two videos, ‘Building the first shape’ and ‘Building the second shape’, Kissmedeadlydoll offers an unpractised and unplanned demonstration of how this off-the-cuff-tying game works and the very different results you can achieve each time you play. She also explains how to play “what if” before adding rope to the body, a fun technique for exploration that doesn’t limit your potential for new shapes.

Finally, Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly share a debrief and feedback session. After all, this game is an opportunity for both riggers and bottoms, to make new shapes and to feel new shapes respectively, and to find new tying pathways together.

This shibari course is aimed at practitioners who already have suspension experience and are looking to get more creative with these skills. Please be mindful of your own skillset when applying any techniques from this collection to your practice.

* Captions available for this series: English
safety: This is a level 4 course that requires significant previous suspension experience from both the person tying and the person being tied. We always suggest learning new sequences with the support of a spotter or with the supervision of a qualified instructor. As this is improvisational play, both partners should have good communication skills, ability to pivot quickly and body awareness.
equipment: At least eight hanks of rope

title: KissmedeadlyDoll's Self-Suspension Chest Harness
description: In this shibari course, KissmedeadlyDoll teaches her Self-Suspension Harness featuring a stable stem behind the back.
about:
As a self-suspender with more than a decade’s experience, Kissmedeadlydoll says she loves taking what people are doing in partnered tying and seeing if she can recreate something similar with self-tying. This Self-Suspension Harness is built for exactly that, with a stable stem behind the back that’s designed for attaching suspension lines and being able to play with back- and side-loading suspension shapes more often seen in partnered ropes.

In the first video, you’ll learn how to tie the harness with step-by-step instructions and some guidelines for easier and less strenuous self-tying. While aimed at more advanced self-tyers, this tutorial is filled with skill-building tips to help you get better at tying behind your back. If the rope handling shown in this tutorial is proving to be a bit out of reach, you can check out Self Tying the Chest for additional tips and tricks on how to make tying behind your back easier.

In the second video, Kissmedeadlydoll details where and how suspension lines can be added to this harness with invaluable advice for self-suspenders to make tying behind the back just that little bit less challenging.

This harness tutorial is aimed at advanced self-tyers who already have some suspension experience. The harness video alone is suitable for less advanced levels but please only attempt to use this tie in suspension if your skill set allows.

title: Gyaku Ebi | Hog Tie
description: In this class Gorgone teaches a 'Hog Tie' form (or Gyaku Ebi). The class is divided in 3 videos for floor, partial and full suspension.
about:
In this class, Gorgone teaches a hogtie form or "Gyaku Ebi" (meaning inverted shrimp in Japanese) with her model Joann. The hogtie is a common method of Shibari restraining all four limbs together behind the body, rendering the subject immobile and totally helpless.

The course is divided into separate classes introducing three variations of this tie for floorplay, partial suspensions and a full transition sequence. In these classes, Gorgone uses her TK3 and Fast Leg-Tie but other alternatives can be used instead.

The floor-based variation is suitable for intermediate level or beginners by replacing the TK with a safer and more simple chest harness. The partial variation is suitable for intermediate-advanced levels.

The transition sequence should be performed by expert practitioners only. It is a challenging transition sequence, combining elements of old-school and modern suspension style.

title: First Partials: Wrist Cuffs
description: In this shibari course, TrueBlue and Margherita explore tying the wrists overhead through a tutorial and demo of a partial suspension.
about:
In this shibari course, TrueBlue and Margherita explore tying the wrists overhead, sharing both a step-by-step tutorial and a demonstration session for one of the first partial suspensions you may learn.

Partial suspensions – ties where part of the body is elevated by rope while other parts remain on the floor – are where you lay the groundwork for exploring suspension in ropes. Or whatever the opposite of groundwork is… It’s here that your rope practice takes flight, which is why it’s so important to get your first partials right. In this class, TrueBlue and Margherita discuss techniques for tying, lifting and loading the wrists as well as your options for locking off. They also offer important safety considerations for tying this sensitive part of the body. As Blue explains, by the time you utilize this tie in play, you should be well practiced in applying, creating uplines and locking them off as well as releasing and untying smoothly and efficiently.

In the first video, you’ll learn how to apply the wrist cuffs as well as load and lock off your upline.

In the second video, TrueBlue and Margherita demo this partial suspension in action, not as a tie-along but to inspire your own explorations.

This partial suspensions-focused course is aimed at intermediate learners who have spent time exploring rope and tension on the body and understand the circulation and nerve risks involved with beginning to play with suspensions.

* Captions available for this series: English
safety: This course is designed to introduce or refresh knowledge of suspension points safety, and upline techniques. It is best practice to be confident in your harness building and floor play before diving into suspension.
equipment: At least two hanks of rope

title: Neko Harness
description: In this class Tamandua teaches the Neko Harness. This harness can be used both for floor play and suspension.
about:
In this class, Tamandua teaches the Neko Harness with his model Mie Neko.

More than just a beautiful hishi tie, this hands-free and beginner-friendly harness is built for sensation-play, all the way from the various pressure points to the stimulating (or threatening) crotch rope. Combine it with other arm ties taught on this site (e.g. Tamandua's Bunny Tie, Strappado, Bamboo Tengu and Teppo, Kinoko's Forearm Binder, Gorgone's Neck-hug or Ladder Tie) for a tie as multifaceted as the gem it’s named after.

This harness is presented here as a floor-play tie but there’s no reason it can’t be used as a suspension go-to if you remove the crotch rope and reinforce the back. We leave it to our most advanced users to figure out the few modifications that might be required to make this harness suspension-worthy and suitable for their partner's unique needs.

title: Booty Basket
description: In this course, Lief and Icky offer a step-by-step class on how to tie their Booty Basket—a fun, versatile, and suspension-ready harness.
about:
GO TO BOOTY BASKET HARNESS GUIDE

In this shibari tutorial, Lief and Icky teach their take on a traditional Booty Basket tie.

An interesting alternative to a gun slinger or hip harness, the booty basket is unique in being a structure that both supports the hips and creates actual restriction. The forced fold of the body at the hips creates very different shapes than traditional hip harnesses. As Lief and Icky explain, they struggled with traditional ways of tying it not offering enough structure and being difficult to tension, so this pattern may be a little different to how you’ve seen it tied before.

In this course, Lief and Icky offer a step-by-step class on how to tie their Booty Basket, for a lower body harness that’s fun on the floor as well as versatile and secure in suspensions. They also teach three different ways of loading the harness for partial suspensions and suspension: from the back, from the side and from the center.

This harness can be utilized in all types of play. However, please keep your skill set in mind and only use it in suspensions if you already have plenty of experience.

title: Bänana's Agura Harness
description: In this shibari tutorial, Bänana teaches her favorite suspendable three-rope Agura Harness with her model Marion.
about:
In this shibari tutorial, Bänana teaches her favorite suspendable three-rope Agura Harness with her model Marion.

The cross-legged Agura is one of those traditional shibari ties that has inspired countless variations, lending itself to adaptations that range from the ultra-simple to the highly structured. Bänana’s Agura? Supportive, robust and designed to be truly versatile in suspensions. As Bänana explains, the key elements of this Agura are a solid, well-reinforced stem to ensure even weight distribution as well as various loading options for taking it into the air. Importantly, she explains how decisions you make at the start of the tie will either make it more or less intense for the person being tied. Start mindfully and follow along to discover what might just become your go-to Agura. (Check out Bänana’s Agura Transition Sequence suspension tutorial to see this harness in action.)

This shibari class is suitable for advanced riggers and bottoms looking for sustainable and stable harnesses for suspension or, if you simply intend to play on the ground, for anyone looking to expand their lower body harness repertoire. Please only attempt to use this harness in suspensions if you already have some suspension experience.

title: Beyond Circus
description: In this course, Fred Hatt teaches two harnesses and a suspension class putting them into use.
about:
In this course, Fred Hatt teaches two harnesses and a suspension class putting them into use with his model Briki.

Dynamic suspension transitions are often associated with ‘circus bondage’ and stage performances, but for Fred this flavour of rope is also a vehicle for ordeal-based play. In this class, he presents his personal approach to playing with suspension transitions that goes beyond simply creating shapes in the air.

The class has a strong focus on the tempo of this kind of scene which is punctuated by a series of peaks (stress positions) and valleys (or ‘pit-stops) of endorphins and adrenaline, distinct from the tempo of semenawa or torment based play, which focuses more on a gradual crescendo towards the apex of a tie.

When doing dynamic suspensions, Fred likes to feed off his partner's impulses, presenting him with choices to provide relief (or ‘pit stops’) for them, or block movement to cause stress. This offers a contrasted experience and rush to the model, always alternating between challenging positions and moments of rest.

He explains how to read the model’s body and make decisions accordingly, the differences between what he calls ‘micro’ and ‘macro’ transitions, blocking movement versus giving room, playing with endorphins and adrenaline.

We recommend learning and practicing the harnesses taught in separate videos prior to watching the full sequence. The harnesses alone are suitable for intermediate level, however the transition class is geared towards advanced-expert level practitioners.

Note that Fred is using a TK in the classes, but you can replace it with a hands-free harness to reduce the risks of nerve damage and stress in the shoulders.

title: Gorgone's Fast Leg Tie
description: In this class, Gorgone teaches her "Fast Futomomo". This leg-tie is designed for faster execution and to reduce the pressure on the shinbone
about:
In this class, Gorgone teaches her "fast leg-tie".

This leg-tie is designed to be executed faster than her Diamond Leg Tie while still avoiding pressure on the shinbone in suspension. The first part of the tie follows a routined pattern but most of the harness is free-form and allows you to adapt the final looks as you wish. In this class, she teaches her Fast Leg-Tie on herself but this tie is suited both for self-suspension and to tie on a partner.

In the suspension line video, she shows how to create a stable anchor point on this leg-tie.

The demo video is a straightforward version of the same tie without talking. It is useful to overview the harness before studying the tutorial or to refresh your memory after you have watched the tutorial with full explanations.

title: Hip Loader
description: This hip harness is mostly used to support the center of gravity to relieve upper body pressure during vertical rope bondage suspensions.
about:
In this class, Gorgone teaches their version of the Hip-Loader with their model Becky.

This minimalistic and wonderfully versatile hip harness is mostly used to support the center of gravity to relieve upper body pressure during vertical suspensions.

It can also be used for a face-down Scorpion Pose, single-point inversions, bridges and face-up torsions. It is the isolated version of the hip-loading block of Gorgone's 'Butterfly Harness' and Gestalta's 'Bamboo TK'.

It can be incorporated in any chest harness with a waist wrap or used separately with any upper body tie – even with a harness that could not be suspended otherwise, such is Kinoko's 'Forearm Binder'.

title: Kinoko’s Updated TK3
description: In this step-by-step shibari course, Kinoko teaches an updated variation of his three-rope TK (takate kote) with his model hua hua.
about:
In this step-by-step shibari course, Kinoko teaches an updated variation of his three-rope TK (takate kote) with his model hua hua.

Good tying is all about adaptation and development – finding what works… and then finding something that maybe works even better. Kinoko’s TK3 has undergone some tweaking, adapting and even simplifying since the early days of Shibari Study when it initially graced our screens as our very first Kinoko-taught tutorial and became a go-to TK for many. In this course, Kinoko not only teaches his modified version in detail, he also explains why, when it comes to safety, the very first knot you tie is also one of the most essential to perfect.

In the first video, Kinoko discusses the role of the hon-musubi or square knot. The knot used to secure the wrists in a TK, the focus of this class is understanding both why this tie is so important as well as how to tie it in such a way that it’s secure, compact and enhances the safety of your TK.

Once your hon-musubi is perfected, it’s time to learn the updated TK3. The second video offers a precise and thorough walk-through of how to tie this chest harness with detailed explanations of Kinoko’s techniques and reasoning. The result? A comfortable TK that’s designed for style, safety and sustainability in suspensions.

This class is suitable for intermediate levels and beyond. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own practice, particularly if you intend to utilize this tie suspensions.

*Captions available for this class: English

As rope crosses the arms in this course, we suggest the person being tied be familiar with how to check their hands for signs of nerve compression.

title: Armbinders For Everyone
description: In this class, Fred Hatt teaches different ways to tie an Armbinder (Strappado).
about:
HARNESS GUIDES: DIAMOND PATTERN, THICK STEM PATTERN

In this class, Fred Hatt teaches different ways to tie an Armbinder with his model Mio.

When tying an Armbinder (or Strappado), it is important to evaluate your partner's flexibility and preference so the tie is adapted to their unique needs. The position of the arms as well as the choice of pattern will vary accordingly. This class aims to give a better understanding of both body and rope mechanics in order to adapt the tie to each new partner and purpose.

Armbinders are challenging ties involving a higher risk of injury than most other harnesses. In this video, Fred explains some of the common sensitive areas and mistakes that could lead to injuries and how to better recognise or avoid them by making the right choices while applying the rope.

The first example is better suited for models with less flexibility, while the second example is better suited for more flexible models looking for a stricter Armbinder. The different technical approaches he presents can hopefully help you understand what type of structure will fit different bodies, and allow you to modify other patterns if needed.

title: Partnered Bamboo Performance
description: In this shibari session, rope partners and lovers Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly share a sweet and spicy bamboo performance.
about:
In this shibari session, rope partners and lovers Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly share a sometimes-sweet, sometimes-spicy Partnered Bamboo Performance, as well as their pre-scene negotiation and post-scene debrief.

Who says shibari has to be serious to be sexy? Definitely not Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly. Coming in (ultra) hot in this connective suspension performance, playful banter, laughter, and tender kisses and nuzzles are as integral to this sequence as, say, toying with vulnerability and exposure, intense waist rope or a fiendish final-minutes crotch rope. Come for the bondage and stay for the bonding!

This performance is suitable for anyone to watch and enjoy. Do let this session inspire you, but please don’t recreate anything you see here unless you are well-practiced in the techniques involved and it is appropriate for your own tying dynamic.

title: Agura Harness
description: In this class, Fred Hatt teaches a suspendable Agura Harness. Modern Shibari refers to any crossed-leg sitting position as Agura Shibari.
about:
In this class, Fred Hatt teaches a suspendable Agura Harness with his model Briki.

Modern Shibari refers to any crossed-leg sitting position as Agura Shibari. For floor play, a simple version of this tie is sufficient but when used for suspensions a more stable structure is necessary. In this video, Fred shows how to tie the Agura with a lot of reinforcements and a solid stem allowing for various anchoring options.

In the suspension video, he demonstrates some of the many possible ways to suspend from this harness. We recommend going back to the ground between the different positions to give your model a rest as this is a fairly intense and challenging tie to be suspended from.

Please feel free to use a different upper-body tie as an alternative to the TK in order to reduce the risk of nerve injury. Recommended harnesses for safer Agura suspensions; Butterfly Harness, Xana Harness, Misungui Harness, Fisherman Harness.

For expert users who wish to spice things up and feel confident using more demanding upper-body structures, you can replace the TK with harnesses like the Neck Hug, Bunny Tie, Tengu or Teppo, for example. If you choose to increase the difficulty by using more challenging chest harnesses, we highly recommend to first experiment with partial suspensions before attempting to fully suspend.

Packed with important upline safety information and advice for what styles and types of ropes best suit her favored techniques, during this course Kissmedeadlydoll shares step-by-step tying instructions for the following lock-offs:

Bottom lock-offs (lock-offs that are close to the body)

Top lock-offs on bamboo

As well as these three lock-offs for self-suspenders, Kissmedeadlydoll offers tips for what to do with your leftover rope as well as answering the all-important question: where to lock off and why?

This course is perfect for self-tyers with plenty of experience tying on the ground looking to begin practicing suspension slowly and smartly. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own rope practice.

title: Dense Rope
description: In this shibari course, hua hua teaches an advanced style of heavy rope bondage she calls Dense Rope with her model Dantianshi.
about:
In this shibari course, hua hua teaches an advanced style of heavy rope bondage she calls Dense Rope with her model Dantianshi.

Heavy bondage is all about intentionally creating intensely restrictive sensations. In ropes, this can mean building up highly compressive ties by applying plenty of rope to the body – hence, ‘dense’ rope. As hua hua explains, this type of bondage is great for people who enjoy the sensations of swaddling or mummification. However, because so much rope is used and the tie takes so long to build, tension control is essential, as is understanding the risks of being in ropes for a significant period of time.

In the first class, hua hua demonstrates how to start this full-body bondage, working up from the feet to the shoulders (or even applying face rope, if desired). As she ties, hua hua also explains the best technique and approach for building up this challenging tie, including tips and tricks for where to place rope joins and how to approach spacing and tension to achieve that maximalist effect. After all, the way you build the tie is key to keeping things as sustainable as possible for as long as possible.

In the second class, the upper body is tied too. As hua hua explains, as you begin to build on the chest, it becomes harder for the person in ropes to breathe comfortably, while the legs are able to withstand more pressure for longer periods. Be mindful with how you approach this tie as it takes a long time to tie and to untie.

This Dense Rope style is recommended for advanced riggers and bottoms only. This type of play should be approached with intention and awareness of the risks involved.

title: TK Lab
description: In this bondage series, Fred explains the principle functions of TKs. This class is ideal for students struggling with finding the right TK
about:
In this class, Fred Hatt explains and deconstructs the principle functions of the two main families of TK with his model Mio.

What is a Takate Kote (TK)? How does it work and what makes it work? Stem or stemless TK: how are they different? What is ‘high hands’ anyway?

In this class, Fred will share some of his insights regarding key aspects of TK mechanics by demonstrating how TK’s vary in their construction across various families. The aim of the class is to help consolidate knowledge and demonstrate how every choice you make in rope is, as in life, a compromise.

By the end of the class, you should realise that every decision in rope is a compromise, and that the existing TK patterns are complete systems designed for the people and the contexts in which they are typically used.

This is a very important class for students who struggle with finding the right TK and need to deepen their understanding of the different types of logic and engineering available to them.

description: In this step-by-step shibari tutorial, Fuoco teaches a Patternless Futomomo with her model Enna.
about:
In this step-by-step shibari tutorial, Fuoco teaches a Patternless Futomomo with her model Enna.

Unlike many other futomomos which rely on a more structured banded pattern to secure the calf to the thigh, this ‘patternless’ variation utilizes more irregular rope placement for a tie that not only looks different to other futomomos, it feels different. As Fuoco explains in the class, this tie is comfortable and great for rope bottoms who might struggle with the pressure on the shin of other banded futomomos. For riggers, taking a less structured approach is also an opportunity to learn to approach tying more intuitively.

This class is intended for beginner levels upward. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own practice.

In this shibari tutorial, Ropunawa teaches his take on the Strappado with his model Freya.

The strappado is a classic arms-behind-the-back tie that delivers on both aesthetics and intensity during tying sessions. As one of Ropunawa’s favorite ties, this exploration of his take on the strappado is full of useful tips for how to effectively tie it on a hyper-flexible model, important information on anatomy and where you can safely apply ropes and pressure on the arms, and how to incorporate and build up this tie in sessions in a way that helps to set and maintain the mood.

This tie is suitable for all students from intermediate level up, however, we recommend you always play with caution and stay aware should any nerve issues arise.

title: Strappado | Armbinders
description: In this class Tamandua teaches two variations of strappado (behind-the-back armbinders).
about:
In this class, Tamandua teaches two variations of strappado (behind-the-back armbinders).

The first variation is easily adaptable for bottoms who may not easily be able to get their elbows close together, while still creating an arm binder that is compact and restrictive. Because this variation of the tie does not support the chest, it’s best utilized for floor-play or partial suspensions only. The second variation with additional wrapping around the chest is suitable for suspensions.

For the suspension line, we recommend using an epsilon on the top wrap for more chest load and eventually add a secondary rope from the wrists to lift the arms. For partial suspensions, you may also attach a rope directly from the wrists with an epsilon for a more extreme variation, as demonstrated in the free Strappado Session demo.

Strappado ties are fairly demanding on the body and involve a higher risk of nerve compression and blood circulation issues – we recommend doing regular hand checks and practicing these ties with extra care.

title: Lavender Harness
description: In this shibari tutorial, Ms Reemah teaches her suspendable Lavender Harness with her model Lavender.
about:
GO TO LAVENDER HARNESS GUIDE

In this shibari tutorial, Ms Reemah teaches her suspendable Lavender Harness with her model Lavender.

The Lavender Harness is the little harness that could – unassuming at first, but with even more potential than its seemingly simple structure may immediately reveal. As Ms Reemah and Lavender explain, the harness was first developed out of a desire to avoid box-ties. The result was a simplified arm binder/TK hybrid that goes big on ease of construction and utility, and minimalist on just about everything else.

In the first part of the course, Ms Reemah shares step-by-step instructions for how to construct the Lavender Harness, including important tips for perfecting your tension – the key ingredient for this tie to work exactly as intended.

In the second part of the course, Ms Reemah expands on just how versatile this harness is in suspensions, demonstrating where it can be loaded from the back, front and sides.

This shibari course is suitable for tying pairs expanding their harness repertoires and looking for alternatives to TKs that prioritize comfort and functionality. Please only attempt the suspension part of the class if you already have some suspension experience.

title: Suspension Points 101 (Free)
description: In this course, Fred Hatt teaches different methods for setting up different Suspension Points.
about:
In this free shibari course, Fred Hatt teaches how to set up a Suspension Point. Learn various methods to create hanging points using props like a sling, a pulley, bamboo, or a carabiner. We recommend watching these videos in the order they are presented here.

The first 'Intro' video is a short introduction covering some safety considerations and an overview of the different options available.

In the video 'Comparing Suspension Points', Fred goes over the differences between using a ring, a bamboo or carabiners for your suspensions. He explains some of the advantages and limitations of each option.

In the video 'Setting Up A Sling', he explains and demonstrates different ways of using a climbing sling to set up a ring or carabiners from a hard point.

In the video 'Setting Up A Bamboo', he explains and demonstrates how to tie off and set up a bamboo for suspensions. Please note that this method requires two separate hard points and should never be installed from a single hard point with both lines coming together in a triangle shape.

In the video 'Using Carabiners', he explains which types of carabiners are safe to use and demonstrates with his model Mio how to use them properly for your uplines. Using carabiners is very different to using a ring or a bamboo because the lines tend to jam and get stuck if not executed properly.

In the video 'Setting Up A Pulley', he teaches how to create a pulley system using a rope and carabiners. This technique is particularly useful for very intense suspensions meant to be short-lived, if you are new to suspensions and want to have an easy way out, or to smoothen out the lifts and drop-downs if your partner is significantly heavier than you.

Please make sure that the hard point(s) you are using when setting up a suspension point is safe and has been installed by a professional or has been tested prior to suspending yourself or a partner.

description: In this class, Gorgone teaches the Cocoon Tie. This surprising tie offers beautiful old-school aesthetics and a very restrictive feeling.
about:
In this class, Gorgone teaches the Cocoon Tie with their model Alma.

This surprising tie is very different from the usually highly engineered harnesses presented by Gorgone, offering beautiful old-school aesthetics and a very restrictive feeling. It can be used for floor play or suspension, and will be particularly appealing to those who enjoy playing with exposure and helplessness.

This tie can be easily modified to suit different bodies or aesthetics, however it can be quite unpredictable in the air and shouldn't be suspended without special attention and care for the possibility of nerve compression or slippage of the wraps over the shoulders.

We recommend experimenting with it in partial suspensions before attempting to suspend fully. You can also use a pulley to lift the whole body at once instead of going up by increments as demonstrated in the class.

The Crab Tie is a classic shibari form that attaches the forearms to the lower part of the legs. From this simple yet highly exposing position the tie can be used for floor play sessions, partial suspensions and even full suspensions. This class is suitable for beginner levels and beyond. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own practice, particularly if you intend to utilize this harness in semi-suspensions or full suspensions.

title: Physical Rope: Suspension
description: In this shibari class, Tifereth continues her 'Physical Rope' series, this time teaching her hands-on style of rope in suspension.
about:
In this shibari class, Tifereth continues her 'Physical Rope' series, this time teaching her hands-on style of rope in suspension with her model Irkalla.

This suspension-focused final installment of Tifereth's 'Physical Rope' series comes with a seemingly simple objective – to “smoosh your partner around between two stable points”. As Tifereth explains, you don’t have to touch even a single upline to create dramatically different shapes and experiences; instead, maximize what you’ve already tied by looking for gaps, utilizing the concepts of ‘leaning’ and ‘stacking’, observing the way the body is already wanting to move, and getting hands-on to help it along. It’s all the fun flips, dynamic action and interpersonal connection of your flashiest suspension sequences, with only a fraction of the work (well, for the rigger anyway). This class? All about learning to do it safely and with a “modicum of grace and style”.

Before you start flinging your tying partner around in space, familiarize yourself with the pre-requisites for this class. It’s essential to have worked your way through both Physical Rope: Ground and Physical Rope: Partials and to deeply understand how the body wants to move on these levels. Both tying partners should have plenty of suspension experience and the person doing the tying should be confident in both the harnesses they choose (more on Tifereth's choices in the class) as well as their suspension lines. Keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from this class and only take your physical rope skills airborne if that is already a part of your rope practice

In this shibari class, Tifereth teaches the Tenshi In Transition with her tying partner Irkalla.

If you’re ready to start exploring the dynamic potential of Tifereth’s iconic made-to-move Tenshi harness, consider this your new mantra: “Control the roll.” Aimed at suspension-experienced riggers and bottoms, this course is all about harnessing Tenshi’s core features: its inherent mobility and potential for collaboratively “sculpting” shapes.

During the class, Tifereth discusses how to control for the pitch of the harness and the different ways to manage your partner’s body in space as you play with this tie; slowly through line management or, if you’re looking to inject more energy into a scene, quickly through hands-on transitions. She also offers valuable tips for where to find stability as well as how to intensify or offload shapes as you play.

This shibari tutorial is for advanced tying partners who are confident in suspensions, particularly as the Tenshi is designed for bottoms who want more mobility in the air. Remember, this is a progressive practice – start slowly and pick up the pace as you become more proficient. Please keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from this class and only use the Tenshi in suspension if that is already a part of your rope practice.

title: Hojo Cuff Deep Dive
description: In this shibari course, Fuoco takes a deep dive into the Hojo Cuff with her model Cat, teaching key techniques, concepts, and drills.
about:
In this shibari course, Fuoco takes a deep dive into the Hojo Cuff with her model Cat.

Hojo cuffs are simply inline single-column ties held together with tension that runs in and tension that runs out, and they can be an incredibly versatile tool to help us avoid unnecessary over-construction of ties. However, to use them effectively, we have to understand how they work and what elements are needed to create bondage that is stable, snug and sustainable. As Fuoco explains, she loves using hojo cuffs for drills and as a learning tool because of what they can teach us about how bodies move and where we can find opportunities to let the fiddly parts of patterns fall away. And whether you’re just learning the ins and outs of hojo cuffs or looking to level up when and how you use them, this course offers something for everybody.

In the first video, you’ll learn what a hojo cuff is with a basic example demonstrating what to keep in mind when tying them and where you might slip up while you’re still getting the hang of them.

In the second video, Fuoco explains the concept of internal tension in the body and how this can be utilized to create more effective and robust hojo cuffs.

The final two videos offer first a lower body challenge and then an upper body challenge. Once you have a confident grasp on the techniques and concepts taught in the first half of the course, these freeform exercises will help you get more creative with your hojo cuff application and realize the (almost) endless possibilities that they offer.

title: Doll’s Bamboo Harness & Booty Basket Sequence
description: In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches Doll’s Bamboo Harness & Booty Basket Sequence with her model Cutebutdeadly.

In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches Doll’s Bamboo Harness & Booty Basket Sequence with her model Cutebutdeadly.

If Doll’s Bamboo Harness has already become one of your favorite upper body ties, this is your chance to elevate it – literally! As Kissmedeadlydoll explains, this suspension sequence is not for beginners or the faint of heart. Combining torsions, upline management and some intentionally challenging moments, it’ll test your skills, confidence and communication, no matter which side of the rope you’re on. Starting with the upper body already tied, a cheeky chest to thigh partial will challenge your bottom’s ability to balance on their tippy toes, before the addition of a booty basket sweeps them off their feet. In the class, Kissmedeadlydoll details all the fun levels and positions you can explore in the air, with pointers for how to dial the intensity both up and down, and plenty of opportunities for sweating, shaking, (consensual) suffering and those all-important booty views.

This demanding sequence is aimed at riggers and bottoms with plenty of suspension experience. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own rope practice.

title: Kinoko’s Fuse Ebi Tie
description: In this shibari tutorial, Kinoko teaches his Fuse Ebi Tie (‘face-down shrimp’ tie) with his model hua hua.
about:
In this shibari tutorial, Kinoko teaches his Fuse Ebi Tie (‘face-down shrimp’ tie) with his model hua hua.

As Kinoko explains, one of the challenges shibari students often encounter in the jump from learning harnesses on the floor to learning how to suspend them is how to maintain balance between left and right. Using Kinoko’s Updated TK3 as a starting point, begin to perfect finding balance in your ties with this floor-based hogtie that uses the body against itself to create some of the same challenges that bottoms will encounter in suspensions. The Fuse Ebi is a tie that demands an equal shape and precise uniform tension on both sides, plus being floor-based, is more sustainable for the person being tied – in short, the perfect tie to practice creating balance before moving on to suspensions. And with its exposing spread-legged position and sustainability making it ideal for foreplay or abandonment play, you might just be able to think of a few other applications for it too…

This class is suitable for intermediate levels and beyond. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own rope practice.

While not playing with breathing itself, this tie does incorporate pressure on the arteries of the neck, so the tutorial includes plenty of essential information on how to tie the neck in a safer way, and how to approach the differences in intensity, practicality, and aesthetics.

The choker tie is a very powerful edge-play experience for both rigger and model but also very tricky to do right, so we insist that students do not try to reproduce this tie unless they have extensive prior experience both with this type of play. title: Microbondage
description: In this shibari course, Anoxia delves into the minutia of Microbondage with their model fuoco.
about:
In this shibari course, Anoxia delves into the minutia of Microbondage with their model fuoco.

What is this, bondage for ants? No, it’s microbondage, the shibari technique dedicated to tying smaller, delicate structures, such as fingers, toes and faces. As Anoxia explains, there are many reasons to tie on this tiny scale. Whether it’s a greater sense of completion as you get to these final details, creating a stronger sense of immobilization, playing with highly sensitive parts of the body or intentionally amplifying certain emotions in a tie, microbondage is a little guy with an outsized impact. In this class series, you will learn two different microbondage techniques as well as tips for safer, smarter tying.

Safety first! Because microbondage focuses on parts of the body that may be more susceptible to injury if tied improperly, the first part of this course is all about important safety considerations. In this class, Anoxia details the risks of microbondage as well as tips for how to mitigate some of these risks.

In videos that follow, Anoxia teaches two approaches to microbondage: through stretch and through pinning. As well as demonstrating how to do each, they also explain when stretch may be more appropriate and when pinning may be more appropriate. Imperative always? Slowing down and bringing awareness to being extra attentive.

This course is appropriate for anyone who already feels confident tying on the macro level (think harnesses, arm binders, leg ties and floor play) and feels ready to zoom in a little. Bottoms should have good body awareness, and clear communication on both sides of the rope is essential.

title: Physical Rope: Ground
description: In this shibari class and demonstration, Tifereth explores techniques for physical rope on the ground with her model Irkalla.
about:
In this shibari class and demonstration, Tifereth explores techniques for physical rope on the ground with her model Irkalla.

One of Tifereth’s favorite ways of tying involves a very physical, hands-on approach on the ground. This technique is less about perfect knots and frictions (or any particular knots and frictions at all) and more about using your rope and body as a tool to press, pull and stretch with intention to push your tying partner to their happy limits.

In the first part of the course, Tifereth demonstrates how just a simple rope can be used to play with body manipulation and feelings of compression, exposure, and more. Her advice? Let go of the idea that you have to tie anything formal and approach from a place of playful exuberance.

In the demonstration video, Tifereth expands on the basic drill taught in the first part of the course, incorporating a slightly more structured approach with only one goal: to make Irkalla feel good, bound and contained in a position that she likes.

The techniques taught in this class can be incorporated into any practice, no matter your level of experience. As Tifereth explains, this is a “partner sport”, so be sure to check in with your tying partner as you set your intentions for this exercise. And do clear some space for play – you’re going to need it.

This is the first of three “Physical Rope” focused courses led by Tifereth. Keep an eye out for “Physical Rope: Partials” and “Physical Rope: Suspension” – coming soon.

Need a comfortable and sustainable hip harness constructed for evenly tensioned suspensions to add to your rope toolkit? Kinoko’s latest go-to might just become yours too. title: Hishi TK
description: In this class, Gestalta teaches two versions of the Hishi TK. The diamonds are created by tying knots along the stem and pulling them apart.
about:
In this class, Gestalta teaches two variations of the Hishi ('diamond') TK with their model Muriel.

The first version is a chest harness only, ending around the waist. The second version goes all the way down through the legs, with the option to separate the wraps around the inner thighs or to keep them running over the crotch.

This pattern follows a different logic than the one used by Kinoko or Gorgone in their diamond-shaped harnesses. Here, the diamonds are created by tying knots along the stem and then pulling them apart instead of building the diamonds in progressive steps with half-hitches and nodomes.

These harnesses are very aesthetically pleasing, but also offer some interesting features for more playful sessions. The pressure points on the front body and increasing tightness as the tie is built make it a perfect structure for Semenawa. It can be used for suspensions or to add a layer of complexity and sensations to your floor-play.

The same anchoring methods can be applied to the full-body version, bearing in mind that the crotch wrap might become tighter according to the position. Make sure to make any adjustments, if necessary.

The full-body variation could be an interesting harness to use on a Hashira (vertical beam) or for a more intense floor-based hog tie, for example!

description: In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches the Kneeling Crotch Predicament partial suspension with her model Cutebutdeadly.
about:
In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches the Kneeling Crotch Predicament partial suspension with her model Cutebutdeadly.

A deviant take on DIY, this spicy predicament sequence opts for a piece of metal pipe as the newest addition to your shibari toolbox to inventively play with balance, stress, stimulation and suffering in a partial suspension. Of course, you can use bamboo too, but there’s something extra fun about hitting up your local hardware store to level up your rope scenes.

In the ‘Prepping The Pipe’ video, Kissmedeadlydoll demonstrates how to prepare your pipe or bamboo before you start your scene in order to minimize fiddling during play.

The session video follows, showcasing both the tie in action as well as step-by-step instructions on how to achieve this strenuous predicament. Watch for options for how to tie the upper body and head as well as how to build up the challenge one small-but-sadistic step at a time.

Finally, Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly offer a debrief and feedback session where they discuss their impressions of the tie. They also share ideas for how to make this challenging partial suspension predicament more painful or more pleasurable, depending on the sensations and emotions you want to bring into your scene.

Elements of this tie can be partially adjusted to fit your own preferences, however, due to its challenging nature, it’s best suited to riggers and bottoms with previous predicament experience. Remember that consent and negotiation are integral to all types of rope play, so check in regularly and remember that play can be stopped at any time.

title: Handling Drills For Uplines
description: In this shibari tutorial series, Fuoco shares a number of follow-along drills for uplines.
about:
In this shibari tutorial series, Fuoco shares a number of follow-along drills for uplines, with exercises designed to help you get your uplines up and down as easily and efficiently as possible.

Confident upline management and control is key to safer suspensions in rope. These handling drills are designed to help you practice and perfect tying smoothly and securely, with or without a partner. Tie along, repeat often and practice regularly, and watch your rope handling transform.

The first drill focuses on smart tying techniques for tying and untying an upline that’s locked with two half-hitches (also known as a clove hitch).

The second drill focuses on tying and untying uplines locked with a slipped overhand knot (also known as a Naka bow).

This rope bondage course is suitable for intermediate levels, particularly if you have already begun exploring suspension. We recommend that everyone spend some time drilling skills for better rope handling, no matter how advanced your practice.

title: Floor Play Flow
description: In this shibari tutorial, hua hua teaches a series of rope flows together with her model Dantianshi.
about:
In this shibari tutorial course, hua hua teaches a series of rope flows together with her model Dantianshi, specifically curated for enjoying all the various sensations and emotions of tying on the floor.

You don’t need complex ties or advanced techniques to create rope scenes filled with intentionality, engagement and emotion. In fact, you don’t even need to move your scenes beyond the floor. In this multi-part course, hua hua explores a variety of floor-based flows and partial suspensions with a focus on making your ropes intentional, maintaining a strong line of communication between both tying partners, and discovering a spectrum of sensations and emotions. Each tie is designed with plenty of room for adaptation and with different intents and styles – some focused on suffering and endurance, others more on eroticism and connection – to better suit various moods, desires and even rope dynamics.

In the Beast Tie sequence, hua hua and Dantianshi demonstrate a simple-yet-sensual floor-based tie that invites a slower pace and softer interactions. The first video focuses on setting the tone for the tie with advice for how to create a more connective or erotic scene. The second part of this class uses a suspension point to gently elevate then hands and feet, allowing for more vulnerability and different options for play.

The Armbinder flow is a sequence with more direct erotic intent. As hua hua explains, deliberate movements and purposeful physical contact are utilized in this tie to convey forcefulness and heighten anticipation and a sense of vulnerability for the person being tied. Take your time too: the gradual pace of this sensual sequence allows plenty of space to build tension and gauge reactions, so giving the person in ropes room to react and choose if they wish to continue or not. hua hua also offers valuable insights for how to build upon this arm binder and create an even more erotically charged rope scene.

In the Shrimp Tie sequence, hua hua explores a classic shibari shape specifically intended to be more strenuous for the person being tied, particularly on the lower back and hips. Beginning with a detailed explanation of how to build the tie using a minimalist TK and an agura, hua hua offers her tips and tricks to make things more or less challenging and ensure that the only stress points in the tie are intentional. Once the tie is constructed, it’s time to play – as hua hua says during this demo sequence, don’t be tempted to start adding things or changing positions immediately but rather sit and observe. It’s a tie that allows you to play with multiple states of mind, sensations and even types of suffering without changing any rope, so give those feelings time to develop and build up for slower, more deliberate semenawa sessions.

This class is suitable, in part, for beginners. However, we recommend some prior experience with uplines before attempting to recreate the partial suspensions in some of these ties. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own rope practice. As hua hua explains, remember to take time to negotiate and discuss what style and intention is suitable for your dynamic. Before beginning to experiment with these ties, decide in advance how you will use them, check in regularly during and remember that play can be stopped at any time if either partner feels uncomfortable.

title: Hands In TK
description: In this shibari course, hua hua explores the possibilities and limitations of the various hand positions available in TKs.
about:
In this shibari course, hua hua explores the possibilities and limitations of the various hand positions available in TKs together with her long-term tying partner Dantianshi.

Where the hands are placed in TKs is a small detail that can make or break your box tie. As hua hua explains, it’s more than just a matter of personal preference – hand placement possibilities will vary from person to person, TK to TK and tie to tie. Whether hands are in or out, low, high or somewhere in the middle will directly influence how your ties look, feel and perform. Understanding which choice to make when will help you create more sustainable and impactful ties – for every bottom and every box.

In the first two videos, hua hua demonstrates a hands-in position, using a stemmed TK, as well as a hands-out position using a stemless TK. Key here is not just that different tie constructions will be more or less suitable for different hand positions, but that there are implications for sensation, mobility and non-verbal expression depending on your choice.

From in and out to high, middle or low, the next two videos are all about which height you place the hands in TK and how that can create vastly different experiences. Demonstrating low and high hand positions, hua hua explains which might be your best choice.

Finally, Dantianshi shares feedback on the different positions – where she felt firmly held, where she felt comfortably at ease, and where she felt uncertain.

This course is suitable for anyone already exploring adapting harnesses rather than learning patterns, and familiar with how load affects harnesses on the body. Please keep your skill set in mind as you apply the concepts taught in this course to your own practice.

The 'Perpendicular Anchor' and 'Vertical Anchor' videos demonstrate two anchor points: one making use of horizontal or perpendicular beams that extend from the top of the vertical beam and one that ties directly onto the vertical beam, meaning that your play can be as varied as your architecture.

For more practiced riggers, Tamandua’s 'Inverted Ebi' gives the classic ebi shape a more demanding twist with an upside-down and compressed semi-suspension that cinches the waist tightly to the beam. title: Agura & Ebi
description: In this class, Gorgone teaches a floor-based Agura & Ebi Shibari with her model Jewelryandfire.
about:
In this class, Gorgone teaches a floor-based Agura & Ebi Shibari with her model Jewelryandfire.

Modern Shibari refers to any crossed-leg sitting position as Agura Shibari. If the upper body is tied and forced close to the open legs, it is called Ebi Shibari (shrimp tie) or Ebi Seme (shrimp torment). The body being bent forward and the knees widely spread, the position resembles the body and tail of a prawn or shrimp.

This classic Shibari is inspired by an ancient method of torture, ebi-zeme (海老責め). If kept for a long period of time, this position will heavily restrict the breathing and generate strong blood flow restrictions creating a burning sensation throughout the entire body.

The modern adaptations of this tie offer safer and less tortuous options, for example by replacing the TK with a less restrictive chest-harness and adapting the severity of the forward bend to your partner's ability and preference. You can play around with different levels of intensity by using either a hands-free harness (easier) or a Strappado (harder).

title: Kinoko's Ketsuzuri
description: In this shibari tutorial, Kinoko teaches two variations of a Ketsuzuri with his model hua hua.
about:
In this shibari tutorial, Kinoko teaches two variations of a Ketsuzuri with his model hua hua.

When it comes to the erotic applications of your shibari skills, suspensions and practical ties for bedroom bondage may – often, rightly – seem worlds apart. However, in this course, Kinoko offers an advanced approach to his Bedroom Bondage, designed for those riggers and models with plenty of suspension experience to be able to apply those skills during intimate play. As he explains in this two-part course, the ketsuzuri shape is perfect for exposure, spanking and ‘people who love butts’.

In the first video, Kinoko teaches a face-down variation of the vulnerable ketsuzuri position, starting with his updated TK3 as a base.

In the second video, Kinoko demonstrates how the same position can be loaded and suspended from the front, so creating a face-up variation – same shape, new angles for exploration!

This class is suitable for advanced practitioners with some suspension experience. Always remember to keep your skill set in mind when applying techniques from any Shibari Study class to your own rope practice. Remember, too, that consent and negotiation are integral to all types of rope play. Before beginning to experiment with these ties, decide in advance how you will use these ties, check in regularly during and remember that play can be stopped at any time if either partner feels uncomfortable.

*Captions available for this class: English

As rope crosses the arms and can be used to intensify the tie, we suggest the person being tied be familiar with hand checks and have good communication skills and body awareness. We always suggest learning new sequences with the support of a spotter or with the supervision of a qualified instructor.

title: Scarlet Letter A
description: In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches her ‘Scarlet Letter A’ floor play predicament with her model Cutebutdeadly.
about:
In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches her ‘Scarlet Letter A’ floor play predicament with her model Cutebutdeadly.

Looking for a chest-opening, legs-opening floor-based tie that’s all about playful torment and maybe not so much about ease, comfort or unrestricted breathing? You’ve come to the right place. The Scarlet Letter A is a tie designed to be more than a little stress-inducing but also a lot of fun, making it an enticing option for experienced tying pairs looking to level up their floor play with elements of exposure, breath play and (optionless) predicament. Using three pieces of bamboo – two longer and one shorter – Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly demonstrates how to achieve this challenging 'A' shape with important insights into the demanding nature of the tie, safety and potential risks involved.

In the introduction video, Kissmedeadlydoll and Cutebutdeadly share their advice on how to approach the tie from both a rigging and bottoming perspective. As they explain, take it slow, don’t overcomplicate things and make sure you have an exit strategy planned, should you need it. Breath play is a powerful type of edge play, and is never without risk. It is essential for both you and your tying partner to understand these risks before attempting to recreate anything you see in these classes. Please remember that you should only follow along with the parts of the class that are within your skill set and risk profile.

In the class video, Kissmedeadlydoll offers a step-by-step tutorial of how to tie the Scarlet Letter A, beginning with a hojo-cuff tengu shape and building up the intensity from there. She also demonstrates an additional even more strenuous position for those bottoms that love a little suffering with their suffering.

description: In this shibari tutorial, Tamandua teaches a shin lacing harness with his model Elio.
about:
In this shibari tutorial, Tamandua teaches a shin lacing harness with his model Elio.

This simple-yet-efficient one-rope tie is designed to capture the lower halves of the legs together, and can be used either for floor play or it can be incorporated into a suspension. Straightforward, minimalist and versatile, careful rope placement and arrangement of the legs – as demonstrated in this class – will also go a long way towards creating a tie that is comfortable and sustainable for models of all body types and levels of flexibility.

This tie is suitable for all levels, but please keep your own practice and skill set in mind and only utilize it for suspension purposes if you already have some experience with suspensions.

title: Flow & Confidence In Hip-Harnesses
description: Self-suspension and dynamic movement class using Gorgone's Hip-Harness.
about:
GO TO GORGONE’S HIP HARNESS GUIDE

In this class, Gorgone teaches her original Hip Harness with her model Becky. Designed from a model's perspective, this Hip-Harness is very well suited for dynamic self-suspensions and partnered suspensions and transitions.

The original tie is particularly well suited for bottoms with more flexibility in the lower back and those who enjoy waist-loaded harnesses. The "wide front" variation demoed on her model Aja is designed to remove all pressure from the waist and lower back for bottoms who prefer hip-loaded harnesses.

The very compact frontal stem gives this harness a very balanced distribution of the load between the three supportive layers and makes it very resistant to dynamic movements in suspension. The placements and tensions are designed to make it as comfortable as possible for inversions and bridge poses.

In the suspension line video, Gorgone shows how to create a stable anchor point. In the Self Suspension class, she demonstrates exercises to help gain confidence and autonomy in a Hip-Harnesses.

The demo video is a straightforward version of the same tie without talking. It is useful to overview the harness before studying the tutorial or to refresh your memory after you have watched the tutorial with full explanations.

title: Running Man
description: In this shibari course, Hajime Kinoko teaches his version of the Running Man suspension with his model hua hua.
about:
In this shibari course, Hajime Kinoko teaches his version of the Running Man suspension with his model hua hua.

Retro dance move or your next favorite vertical suspension? The ‘Running Man’ suspension is tied from standing to create an upright shape with one bent leg raised in front and the other bent behind – sort of a mid-sprint, but in ropes!

However, as you’ll learn, upright doesn’t necessarily mean easy. As Kinoko explains, for this tie to work you need to carefully maintain position and balance with meticulous tying, tension and body manipulation, all of which he demonstrates in detail in the class. Get it wrong and you’ll struggle with tilting, uneven load distribution and a difficult-to-maintain tie… Get it right and you’ll have a beautiful and well-balanced Running Man worthy of Kinoko himself.

This class is aimed at advanced learners looking for a new vertical suspension shape that’s as rewarding as it is challenging. We recommend that both tying partners have plenty of suspension experience.

It can be used in the same fashion for single-point inversions or in combination with a loaded chest harness to create various positions and transitions, as demonstrated in the Suspension video. title: Kinoko's Hip Harness
description: In this class, Hajime Kinoko teaches his Hip Harness for suspension.
about:
In this class, Hajime Kinoko teaches his Hip Harness for suspension with his model Maya Homerton.

Function meets form in this intermediate level harness. Kinoko’s hip harness is designed in such a way that it enables comfortable suspensions for every body types without demanding a high level of flexibility.

It offers sturdy hip support and reduces waist load (as opposed to Gorgone’s hip-harness designed for models with more back flexibility and who enjoy waist load), making it ideal if you’re looking to take some pressure off the lower back in bridge positions. This versatile tie is ideal for inversions and bridges and is solid enough to sustain dynamic transitions and self-suspensions.

Further information regarding the suspension line:

Kinoko's suspension line method for this tie is very simplified to allow the rigger to attach it easily and quickly during transition work (e.g. while the model is in a face-down and needs support quickly) and prioritizes efficiency over symmetry and balance. If you prefer, you can also use a normal Epsilon instead of the anchoring demonstrated in this tutorial.

title: Doll’s Bamboo Harness
description: In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches two version of Doll’s Bamboo Harness, her suspendable chest and arm harness.
about:
In this shibari class, Kissmedeadlydoll teaches two version of Doll’s Bamboo Harness, her suspendable chest and arm harness, with her models Cutebutdeadly and Mickael.

Incorporating the arms, chest and a length of bamboo, this harness is a great option to bind the arms for those looking for alternatives to box ties. Go more minimalist or build in a little more support – as Kissmedeadlydoll explains, it can be adapted depending on your bottom’s needs.

In the first video, Kissmedeadlydoll demonstrates the base pattern of the tie on Cutebutdeadly, followed by a third rope-inspired front lock-off variation.

The second class picks up with the base pattern taught in the first video now tied on Mickael, however, this time with a variation designed to offer more anchoring for the wraps. As Kissmedeadlydoll explains, this can be helpful for bottoms with more rounded shoulders and bigger bodies or for those who prefer more support.

The final video shows how to add a hanger to the back of the harness for suspension purposes. (While it can be loaded from the back or side, Kissmedeadlydoll says that most people prefer it from the back, but feel free to experiment if it’s within your skill set.)

As this harness is designed for suspension, this tutorial is aimed at advanced riggers and bottoms who already have some suspension experience. Less advanced levels may be able to tie along but please only attempt to use this tie in suspension if your skill set allows.

description: In this shibari tutorial, Gigi demonstrates how to tie a Reverse TK on their model Cait.

In this shibari tutorial, Gigi demonstrates how to tie a Reverse TK on their model Cait.

Unlike many TKs, which can be difficult to sustain for long periods, particularly in suspensions, this arms-in-front ‘Reverse TK’ is designed for comfort.

In the first video, Gigi demonstrates how to tie the harness, detailing the ways in which it is engineered to be more sustainable for bottoms, from the frictions placed on the front of the harness to the third band for extra support. This harness is suitable for models of all body types and levels of flexibility, with its construction allowing for numerous options for loading, making it an ideal choice for bigger bodied bottoms wanting more support to stay in the air through transitions in suspensions.

In the second video, Gigi discusses how this tie can be loaded for suspensions, with three different options: in front for face-up suspensions, on the side, and on the back for face-downs.

The harness part of this tie is suitable for students of all levels, however, please only attempt to suspend from this harness if your skill set allows it and you have some prior suspension experience.

In this class, Tamandua teaches a Tengu and Waist Predicament with his model Elio.

This face-up partial suspension uses a slightly modified Tengu pattern as its basis, accentuating the open posture of the chest with a hip opening cross-legged stance for the legs for a position that, while accessible for many body types and levels of flexibility, is exposing and plays with vulnerability too. The Tengu harness is adapted to allow front loading without pulling on the neck for a more sustainable tie, while waist rope turns up the intensity in the final position.

This tutorial can be adapted for TKs or any other type of chest harness structure that supports front loading. It’s the perfect entry to elevating your floor play a little bit at a time.

title: Tenshi Suspension
description: In this shibari class, Ropunawa teaches the chest-free Tenshi Harness Suspension with his model Freya.
about:
In this shibari class, Ropunawa teaches the chest-free Tenshi Harness Suspension with his model Freya. The Tenshi was originally developed by Tifereth and is taught here with her permission.

In the follow-up to his class on the unconventional Tenshi Harness, Ropunawa delves further into the utility of this ingenious tie by demonstrating a full suspension with the tenshis. By lifting the Tenshi Harness to standing and then incorporating a Basket Tie to support the lower body, the chest-free harness can be used to create an eye-catching side suspension. From here, Ropunawa further explains various tricks to play with different heights, as well as showing how the tenshis can be brought to the front for an even more drastic change and evidence of the tie’s surprising versatility.

As with every tie though, the Tenshi Harness Suspension is not without its own important technique and safety considerations. Both riggers and models alike should be well-practiced in suspensions before attempting this class.
